compiled_state.description:
Store only the SET of Jira keys seen last pass instead of the full ACLI payload. prev_snapshot is
**228.1 MB / 4.5 MB per day** — the largest term after A1. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Measured effect
Over the newest **400 real revisions**: **218 of 399** consecutive pairs have an **identical key
set** (so they become byte-identical and produce no commit at all), and when it changes the mean
symmetric difference is **1.78 keys**. Key-set payload at HEAD is **19,960 bytes** vs a **27.1 MB**
full payload.

## Why this is safe — gate G1 was cleared empirically, not by reasoning
A corpus mutation-diff ran the real differ over **four real snapshot pairs** with full prev vs
key-set prev and found **zero difference in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect**.
The feared `_compute_mutations_emit_both` field-clearing does not reach Jira:
`_mutation_to_batch_dict` reads `payload["changed_fields"]` for updates, which branch-3 never sets,
so `fields` collapses to `{}` and `update_issue(key)` short-circuits at `acli.py:181-185` with zero
subprocess and zero network.

**It also removes a latent bug.** With today's full prev, keys in prev-but-not-curr emit
`(outbound, create)` carrying the departed issue's raw field blob — and that payload shape DOES reach
`create_one`. Corpus: **973-998 spurious Jira creates** whenever the fetch window shrinks or the
project is re-targeted. A key-set emits none.

Shape constraint: store a **dict** `{jira_key: {}}`, not a `set` — `check_dual_identity_complete`
and `_emit_both`'s `local_state[key] or {}` guards assume dict entries.

## Rollback (mandatory artifact)
The G1 corpus diff ran **forward only**. Before merging, run it **backward** (key-set -> full, the
revert direction) and record the result. Deleting `prev_snapshot.json` is **not** a safe default
escape hatch: an empty prev is exactly what made the differ re-derive 2050+ inbound creates every
pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`), because `differ.py:455-490` emits an inbound CREATE for every
curr-only key unless a `rebar-id:` label suppresses it — bound pairs are safe, unbound in-window keys
are not. If deletion is ever used, it MUST be followed by a cap-0/no-write pass proving zero inbound
creates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over **>=4 real snapshot pairs** shows **zero
      difference** in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect. Tier: **repo-level corpus
      script** committed under the experiments path.
- [ ] The **reverse-direction** diff (key-set -> full) is recorded on this ticket as the rollback
      artifact, showing the revert path emits no unexpected inbound creates. Tier: **repo-level
      corpus script**.
- [ ] Branch-2 regression is gone: with a key-set prev and >=900 prev-only keys, **zero**
      `(outbound, create)` mutations are emitted. Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations`.
- [ ] `check_dual_identity_complete` and the binding-walk adopt-skip set behave identically with
      `{}` entries. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] prev_snapshot at HEAD is <=64 KB after one pass. Verify: byte measurement.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` (prev persist),
`run_differs.py`, tests, corpus script

Scope: M. Depends on A4-1.
